To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there are many different types of bacteria that can cause typhoid fever, and that some of the bacteria are resistant to common antibiotics.
the incidence of typhoid fever has decreased in the last 10 years in India, but it still remains a major cause of mortality and morbidity in the country.
the incidence of typhoid fever has decreased in children in the age group 1-5 years in Delhi and that the incidence of MDRTF is increasing in the same age group.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: a) to determine the frequency of Salmonella typhi in stool and blood of patients of suspected enteric fever b) to determine the sensitivity pattern to first line and alternative antibiotics. c) To determine the frequency of MDRTF in our area.
the development of a rapid diagnostic test for typhoid fever.
the following: (1) To find the prevalence of Salmonella Typhi in children of different age groups in our community.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of ampicillin, cotrimoxozale and chloramphenicol should not be recommended for empirical treatment of typhoid fever.
the current first line drugs are not effective against typhoid fever.
the use of first line drugs is not recommended in children with typhoid fever.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no need to change the current guidelines of treating typhoid fever with first line drugs unless the sensitivity report shows the organisms to have resistance to these drugs.
the treatment of typhoid should be based on the antibiotic sensitivity testing of the isolated organism.
we need to be more aggressive and vigilant about the treatment of typhoid fever and not just rely on the drugs that are easily available.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a need for more research to understand the reasons for the re-emergence of fully sensitive Salmonella typhi strains and also to study the clinical outcomes of patients treated with these fully sensitive strains.
there is a definite need to do antibiotic sensitivity testing of Salmonella Typhi before prescribing antibiotics for typhoid fever.
we should be careful in treating typhoid fever in children.
